description: This method searches for a cheap plan of a SAS+ planning task (a task over multi-valued state variables and operators with preconditions, effects and costs) with a steady-state genetic algorithm. A genome is a variable-length chain of operator ids. To decode it, the method simulates the task from the initial state: by default it skips each operator that is not applicable (*phenotypic repair*) and stops at the first goal state. A valid plan costs its plan cost. An invalid chain costs a large penalty plus the number of unsatisfied goal facts plus the fraction of the chain that does not execute, so near-misses rank above far misses (a *fitness cascade*). Optionally, *genotypic repair* writes the executed plan back into the chain. Every returned plan is valid, but it is not guaranteed to be optimal; use it when a valid plan is enough or as a baseline for heuristic search.
